rows.text: March 8, 2007
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
In the real economy, exports continue to show steady growth, facilities and construction investment maintains a robust growing pace.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
On the other hand, private consumption exhibits a slowdown in the pace of its expansion.
Meanwhile, the current account has recorded a deficit, owing mainly to the narrowed goods account surplus.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
In the real economy, exports continue to show steady growth, facilities and construction investment maintains a robust growing pace.
Consumer price inflation and core inflation both remain stable.
The upward pace of real estate prices has slowed down.
On the other hand, private consumption exhibits a slowdown in the pace of its expansion.
Meanwhile, the current account has recorded a deficit, owing mainly to the narrowed goods account surplus.
In the financial markets, financial institutions' lending has slowed the pace of its expansion.
Consumer price inflation and core inflation both remain stable.
Nevertheless, overall liquidity conditions are favorable.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the call rate target (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
